text:
## Description

The Python 3 program reads the initial tooth lengths and the permitted difference between adjacent upper teeth from standard input. It prints the minimum total cost in yen to make the teeth fit together well.

## Preconditions

- **PRE-1 — Unverified.** The first input line contains integers \(N\) and \(X\), with \(2 \le N \le 200{,}000\) and \(1 \le X \le 10^9\).
- **PRE-2 — Unverified.** The next \(N\) lines give one pair of integer lengths in left-to-right order. Each line gives the upper length \(U_i\) followed by the lower length \(D_i\), both in \([1,10^9]\).

## Postconditions

- **POST-1 — Unverified.** In any reachable final configuration, every tooth has an integer length between zero and its initial length, inclusive, and retains its position. Each operation reduces exactly one positive tooth length by one at a cost of one yen.
- **POST-2 — Unverified.** A reachable configuration fits together well exactly when every upper–lower pair has the same total length and every pair of adjacent upper teeth differs in length by at most \(X\). Equality at \(X\) is allowed.
- **POST-3 — Unverified.** Standard output contains one integer equal to the minimum total cost among all reachable configurations that fit together well. Grinding all teeth to zero is always feasible, so the minimum exists. The answer is zero exactly when the initial configuration already fits, and values beyond the 32-bit signed integer range are printed exactly.

## Test suggestions

- Use two pairs \((3,1)\) and \((1,3)\) with \(X=2\) and expect `0`. Repeat with \(X=1\) and expect `1` to check the inclusive adjacency limit and the need to grind even when pair totals already agree (PRE-1, PRE-2, POST-2, POST-3).
- With \(X=2\), compare the order \((1,3),(2,2),(4,0+1)\) only after choosing valid positive initial lengths. For a direct check, use \((1,4),(2,3),(4,1)\) and expect `0`, then move \((2,3)\) to the end and expect `1` (PRE-2, POST-2, POST-3).
- Check that the third sample prints `5999999994` exactly (POST-3).

## Unspecified behavior

- Behavior for malformed input or values outside the stated constraints.
- Which optimal configuration or sequence of grinding operations is chosen when several attain the same minimum.

isolation.limits: Codex harness instructions and its own tool descriptions remain in the model context; they cannot be removed. Tool isolation is verified post hoc from the event stream, which contained no tool, command, file or search events.
